verses: Jesus also said to them, “Does anyone bring in a lamp to put it under a basket or under a bed? Doesn’t he set it on a stand?
For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be brought to light.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”
He went on to say, “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured to you, and even more will be added to you.
For whoever has will be given more. But whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.”
Jesus also said, “The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground.
Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how.
All by itself the earth produces a crop—first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within.
And as soon as the grain is ripe, he swings the sickle, because the harvest has come.”
Then He asked, “To what can we compare the kingdom of God? With what parable shall we present it?
It is like a mustard seed, which is the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.
But after it is planted, it grows to be the largest of all garden plants and puts forth great branches, so that the birds of the air nest in its shade.”
With many such parables Jesus spoke the word to them, to the extent that they could understand.
He did not tell them anything without using a parable. But privately He explained everything to His own disciples.
When that evening came, He said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side.”
After they had dismissed the crowd, they took Jesus with them, since He was already in the boat. And there were other boats with Him.
Soon a violent windstorm came up, and the waves were breaking over the boat, so that it was being swamped.
But Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion. So they woke Him and said, “Teacher, don’t You care that we are perishing?”
Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the sea. “Silence!” He commanded. “Be still!” And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm.
“Why are you so afraid?” He asked. “Do you still have no faith?”
Overwhelmed with fear, they asked one another, “Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?”
title: All by Itself
season_line: Still by the Sea of Galilee after the parable of the sower, Jesus tells a few more seed stories, then takes His friends out onto the water as night falls.
big_idea: You plant and you tend, but God gives the growth, and the One who grows it also rules the storm.
frame: Raising children is mostly sowing seed you won't see sprout for years. You pray, you correct, you read the same Bible story for the fortieth time, and most days you can't tell if any of it is taking root. Jesus says the kingdom works that way: real growth, hidden from view, by God's power and not ours. Paul said the same about his ministry in {{1 Corinthians 3:6-7|1 Corinthians 3:6–7}}: people plant and water, but God makes things grow. So carry two things into today. Be faithful in the small, ordinary sowing, and let go of the anxious need to control the harvest. And when the waves come with a child, remember who is in the boat with you.

carry.text: Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how.

glance.head: A Lamp on a Stand
glance.line: What Jesus is teaching won't stay hidden, so listen closely, because those who take it in will be given more.

glance.head: The Seed Grows Secretly
glance.line: A farmer sows, sleeps, and wakes, and the seed grows by itself until harvest.

glance.head: The Mustard Seed
glance.line: God's kingdom starts tiny but grows large enough to give shelter to many.

glance.head: Wind and Waves Obey
glance.line: Jesus sleeps through a storm, then silences it with a word, leaving His friends asking who He really is.

understand: Yesterday Jesus told the parable of the sower and explained it privately to the Twelve. Today He adds more short pictures. A lamp isn't meant to be hidden: the meaning tucked inside these parables will come to light. And the way we listen matters. Those who lean in and receive what He says will be given more understanding; those who shrug it off lose even what they had.

The seed that grows by itself appears only in Mark. The farmer does real work, sowing and harvesting, but the growing in between is out of his hands and beyond his understanding. The mustard seed makes a similar point from another angle: the kingdom looks small and unimpressive now, a carpenter and a few fishermen, but it will become great. Birds nesting in its branches echo Old Testament pictures of a kingdom that shelters the nations, like {{Ezekiel 17:22-24|Ezekiel 17:22–24}}.

Then the lesson moves from the field to the sea. The Sea of Galilee sits low among hills, and sudden storms can sweep down on it. Notice the link to the seed story: the farmer sleeps while God works, and now Jesus sleeps while the storm rages. His rest isn't neglect. It's perfect trust in His Father.

When He rises, He rebukes the wind just as He rebuked an unclean spirit in {{Mark 1:25|Mark 1:25}}. In the Old Testament, only God rules the raging sea ({{Psalm 89:9|Psalm 89:9}}; {{Psalm 107:23-30|Psalm 107:23–30}}). That's why the disciples end more afraid than they started. They are beginning to see that the man in their boat is the Lord Himself.

word.gloss: This Greek word is where our word 'automatic' comes from. It means the growth happens without the farmer's effort or control; God's power is at work in the soil.

glow: All by itself the earth produces a crop
Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?

god.short: Pray verse 27 over each child by name, handing their growth to God.
god.full: Name each child you love before God (your own, grandkids, nieces or nephews) and pray, 'You grow what I can't see in them.' Then let go of one specific worry about how fast they're changing.
god.why: Paul planted and Apollos watered, but God gave the growth ({{1 Corinthians 3:6-7|1 Corinthians 3:6–7}}).

together.short: Tell each other one small sign of growth you've noticed in a child.
together.full: Before you part this morning, each of you name one tiny sprout you've seen in a child lately, like a kind word, an honest confession, or a question about God.

others.short: Text a weary parent you know that their unseen sowing matters.
others.full: Think of a parent who is tired or discouraged right now. Send a short note telling them the ordinary things they do every day are seed that God is growing, even if they can't see it yet.
others.why: The kingdom starts as the smallest seed and still grows large ({{Mark 4:31-32|Mark 4:31–32}}).

tonight: Where are we trying to force growth in our kids, or in the young people around us, that only God can give, and what would faithful sowing look like there instead?

more.line: We plant and water; God gives the growth.
